title: Emergency traffic shift reconciliation and runbook gaps after asymmetric region degradation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 we received escalations from two enterprise customers reporting elevated 5xx errors and end-user timeouts after automated traffic steering moved load off a degraded Europe-west region into mixed Hosted/Dedicated capacity. Investigation showed inconsistent routing + KV cache drift between dedicated pools and hosted fallback nodes which resulted in repeated cold-starts, cache thrashing, and tokenization errors for some model variants. This ticket tracks the emergency mitigation, short-term customer remediation, root cause analysis, runbook gaps, and full bugfix rollout plan.
impact_details: Affected: 2 enterprise customers on Dedicated pools with cross-region routing policies. Symptom: ~15% error rate spike, 95th percentile latency increased from 210ms to 1.3s for affected routes. Duration: incident window ~2026-03-10T03:10Z to ongoing partial degradation. Secondary impact: failed fallback to hosted API caused increased quota pressure and temporary client rate limiting for some orgs.
customers_escalated: Acme Health (account-id: acme-123), FinWave Corp (account-id: fin-987)
incident_timeline: 2026-03-10T02:58Z - Automatic region health probe flagged increased error rate in eu-west node group and initiated traffic-shift policy.
2026-03-10T03:05Z - Traffic steering moved 60% of eu-west traffic to dedicated pools in eu-central and hosted clusters in us-west.
2026-03-10T03:12Z - Customer support received first escalations from Acme Health about timeouts; SRE triage paged.
2026-03-10T03:30Z - Ops applied temporary routing cap to limit burst to hosted fallback; short-term mitigation reduced errors for some routes but not all.

2026-03-10T04:00Z - Engineering reproduced error: KV cache key mismatch in dedicated pools when requests were routed mid-session to hosted fallback; deduplication tokens failed causing structured output errors.
2026-03-10T06:20Z - Hotfix PR opened to add cache-invalidation step to the regional failover orchestration (PR #6452).
2026-03-10T09:40Z - Ops performed coordinated rolling restart of proxy process in dedicated pools to flush stale routing tables; observed partial recovery.
2026-03-11T14:00Z - Continued reconciliation work; ticket opened to update runbook and add synthetic checks for cross-environment cache consistency.
mitigation_performed: Immediate: throttled redirects to hosted fallback, added ingress rate caps for affected orgs, applied rolling proxy restarts in dedicated pools to evict stale routing entries. Short-term code change: backported cache-invalidation hook into failover path (PR #6452) and deployed to canary before wider rollout. Customer-level remediation: temporary increased quota and manual routing pin for Acme Health while we stabilize.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate eu-west node-group high-latency by injecting 100-200ms delay on health probe; 2) Trigger traffic-steering policy to move subset of sessions to another region; 3) Observe dedicated pool session routing when fallback to hosted occurs mid-request; 4) Check KV cache keys for model_context_id mismatch and inspect 5xx logs for tokenization exceptions.
root_cause: Primary cause: orchestration failover path omitted a mandatory KV/cache reconciliation step when moving in-flight sessions between Dedicated and Hosted targets. Secondary contributors: stale proxy routing tables in dedicated clusters and insufficient synthetic coverage for cross-environment session continuity. Edge case: some model variants used different serialization schema which caused tokenization errors when the fallback node hosted a slightly different model build.
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Add an atomic cache reconciliation + soft-evict step into the failover orchestrator (runtime change). 2) Enhance proxy startup to validate routing table hashes and auto-reconcile with control plane. 3) Add pre-failover checks to ensure fallback model variant compatibility; auto-fallback to compatible variant when mismatch is detected. 4) Expand synthetic tests to include cross-region session handoffs with both Hosted and Dedicated topologies.
runbook_changes_required: - Insert explicit 'invalidate-session-prefixes' step before traffic redirection. - Add checklist to verify model-variant compatibility and K/V namespace alignment. - Add escalation path: phone/pager + SRE lead + dedicated account engineering contact. - Include rollback play: throttle traffic at edge + resume prior region routing. New runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/cross-region-reconciliation-draft
test_plan: Unit + integration tests for cache reconciliation logic; e2e synthetic that simulates region degradations on canary; chaos test to force mid-request routing switch between hosted and dedicated with assert for zero 5xx. Add nightly synthetic that exercises each org's Dedicated-hosted fallback path.

postmortem_plan: Complete RCA write-up, include timeline and decision logs, quantify customer SLA impact, publish to Confluence, host postmortem review with SRE/Runtime/CS within 7 days. Identify compensating credits for impacted customers and assign ACV owner for outreach.
customer_communication: Initial incident notification sent by CS at 2026-03-10T05:10Z. Follow-up email template in Confluence. Assignments: Nora Alvarez to lead customer follow-ups; legal looped for potential contract impact.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Failover path includes reconciliation hook and is covered by unit + integration tests. 2) Synthetic cross-env tests pass in staging for 48h. 3) Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE + Runtime + CS. 4) No repeat of error spike in 2 weeks during scheduled cross-region failover simulation.

2026-03-12: Design review suggested adding explicit telemetry for session-variant mapping; accepted and added to runtime PR.
2026-03-13: Security reviewed surface area for cache-invalidation hook; no PII exposure risk identified.
